options.text: Having no alleles for a gene
Having only one allele for a gene
Having two identical alleles for a gene
Having two different alleles for a gene

questions.explanation: Homozygous means having two identical alleles for a particular gene. This can be homozygous dominant (e.g., BB) or homozygous recessive (e.g., bb). The organism is described as a 'pure breed' for that characteristic.

questions.stem: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?

options.text: Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the genetic makeup
They mean the same thing
Genotype is the genetic makeup; phenotype is the observable characteristic
Genotype refers to dominant alleles only; phenotype refers to recessive alleles

questions.explanation: The genotype is the combination of alleles an organism has (e.g., Bb). The phenotype is the observable characteristic that results from the genotype (e.g., brown eyes). The phenotype is determined by the genotype and sometimes the environment.

questions.stem: A person with the genotype Bb is described as:

options.text: Homozygous recessive
Homozygous dominant
Heterozygous
Codominant

questions.explanation: Heterozygous means having two different alleles for a particular gene (e.g., Bb). In this case, the dominant allele (B) determines the phenotype, and the individual is a carrier of the recessive allele (b).

options.text: An allele that is always expressed, even when only one copy is present
An allele that is only expressed when two copies are present
An allele that causes disease
An allele that is more common in the population

questions.explanation: A dominant allele is always expressed in the phenotype when present, even if only one copy is inherited (heterozygous). It is represented by a capital letter (e.g., B). It 'masks' the effect of the recessive allele.

questions.stem: When is a recessive allele expressed in the phenotype?

options.text: When one copy is present
Only when two copies are present (homozygous recessive)
It is never expressed
When it is on the X chromosome

questions.explanation: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when an individual has two copies (homozygous recessive, e.g., bb). In heterozygous individuals (Bb), the dominant allele masks the recessive allele's effect.

questions.stem: What is a carrier in genetics?

options.text: A protein that transports alleles
A person who shows symptoms of a genetic disorder
A person who is heterozygous for a recessive allele but does not show the trait
A chromosome that carries genes

questions.explanation: A carrier is a heterozygous individual who has one copy of a recessive allele but does not show the recessive trait because the dominant allele masks it. Carriers can pass the recessive allele to their offspring.

options.text: When one allele completely masks the other
When a trait is controlled by multiple genes
When neither allele is expressed
When both alleles are expressed equally in the phenotype

questions.explanation: Codominance occurs when both alleles are expressed equally in the phenotype of a heterozygous individual. Neither allele is dominant over the other. An example is the ABO blood group system, where alleles A and B are codominant.
